cards.title: Signed Ising objective
cards.role: Defines every independently generated benchmark instance and its exact objective.

checks.detail: The signed Ising Hamiltonian, cubic graph ensemble, and J=±1 domain are explicit in Eq. (14) and the Fig. 1 caption.
Each generated graph has 3n/2 edges, degree three at every vertex, and only signed unit weights.

open_questions: The paper does not publish the 32 graph/coupling instances or their random seeds.

cards.title: Level-1 QAOA state and approximation ratio
cards.role: Defines the blue-bar variational expectation divided by the exact Ising maximum.

checks.detail: The state order and variational objective are explicit in Appendix A; the denominator is explicit in the Fig. 1 caption.
At fixed gamma the energy is A sin^2(2 beta)+B cos(2 beta)sin(2 beta), whose global beta maximum is analytic.
The zero-gap MILP optimum agrees with exhaustive enumeration on a signed 8-spin cubic graph.

cards.role: Computes every QAOA energy term and every RQAOA rounding correlation without a quantum simulator.

checks.detail: Every factor and sign is transcribed from Appendix C Eq. (C9), with gamma restored by J→gamma J as stated below the lemma.
All active-edge correlations agree with direct four-qubit statevector evolution to 2e-12.
Integer couplings make gamma in [0,pi] a complete period after recursive contractions.

cards.title: RQAOA correlation rounding
cards.role: Eliminates one variable and merges its incident couplings into the retained variable.

checks.detail: The maximum-correlation choice, sign constraint, coupling substitution, and recursive cutoff are explicit in the main text and Appendix C pseudocode.
At every completed recursion, reconstructed original energy equals reduced optimum plus accumulated constant shift.
The recursion stops at n_c=8 for n=32 and n_c=30 for n=100.

open_questions: The paper permits arbitrary tie breaking; this case deterministically chooses the first maximum in sorted edge order.

cards.title: Exact Ising normalization
cards.role: Normalizes both algorithms by a separately proved exact optimum.

checks.detail: The exact maximization denominator and algorithm-output ratio are stated in the Fig. 1 caption.
With d_uv=b_u XOR b_v, J_uv z_u z_v=J_uv(1-2d_uv), giving the binary MILP objective.
Final runs require solver success and zero reported MIP gap.
